sanskrit: amātyānāṃ yadi kāmasya hetor; evaṃyuktaṃ karma cikīrṣasi tvam apākrameḥ saṃpradāya svam ebhyo; mā gās tvaṃ vai devayānāt patho 'dya
english: If it is for the sake of the ministers' desire that you intend to do a deed so arranged, then withdraw after handing over your own to them — do not today, I tell you, stray from the path that leads to the divine.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca asaṃśayaṃ saṃjaya satyam etad; dharmo varaḥ karmaṇāṃ yat tvam āttha jñātvā tu māṃ saṃjaya garhayes tvaṃ; yadi dharmaṃ yady adharmaṃ carāmi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Without doubt, Saṃjaya, what you have said is true — dharma is the highest of all deeds. But having known me, Saṃjaya, you censure me; whether I practise dharma or adharma, you reproach me.

sanskrit: yatrādharmo dharmarūpāṇi bibhrad; dharmaḥ kṛtsno dṛśyate 'dharmarūpaḥ tathā dharmo dhārayan dharmarūpaṃ; vidvāṃsas taṃ saṃprapaśyanti buddhyā
english: In a situation where adharma, wearing the guise of dharma, appears entirely as dharma in adharma's form, and where dharma, bearing the form of dharma, the wise perceive it clearly with their discernment —

sanskrit: evam etāv āpadi liṅgam etad; dharmādharmau vṛttinityau bhajetām ādyaṃ liṅgaṃ yasya tasya pramāṇam; āpaddharmaṃ saṃjaya taṃ nibodha
english: Thus, in adversity, these two — dharma and adharma — who are eternally present in conduct, share the same outward mark. The first mark of whichever one is present is the standard; understand that, Saṃjaya, as the dharma of adversity.

sanskrit: luptāyāṃ tu prakṛtau yena karma; niṣpādayet tat parīpsed vihīnaḥ prakṛtisthaś cāpadi vartamāna; ubhau garhyau bhavataḥ saṃjayaitau
english: When one's normal mode of living has been disrupted, the destitute man should seek to accomplish the deed by which he can restore it; yet both the man who, despite being in his normal state, acts in adversity's mode, and the man already destitute who persists in it — both are blameworthy, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: avilopam icchatāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ; prāyaścittaṃ vihitaṃ yad vidhātrā āpady athākarmasu vartamānān; vikarmasthān saṃjaya garhayeta
english: For brāhmaṇas who desire the preservation of their duties, the Creator has prescribed expiation; but in adversity one should censure those who engage in forbidden acts and stand in wrong conduct, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: manīṣiṇāṃ tattvavicchedanāya; vidhīyate satsu vṛttiḥ sadaiva abrāhmaṇāḥ santi tu ye na vaidyāḥ; sarvocchedaṃ sādhu manyeta tebhyaḥ
english: For the purpose of imparting true understanding to the wise, conduct among the good is always prescribed; but as for those who are not brāhmaṇas and not learned — from them one should consider total severance to be the right course.

sanskrit: tadarthā naḥ pitaro ye ca pūrve; pitāmahā ye ca tebhyaḥ pare 'nye prajñaiṣiṇo ye ca hi karma cakrur; nāsty antato nāsti nāstīti manye
english: For that very purpose our fathers of old, and the grandfathers, and those others yet further back who sought wisdom and performed their deeds — I believe that in the end there is nothing, nothing, nothing for them.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cid etad vittam asyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ; yad devānāṃ tridaśānāṃ paratra prājāpatyaṃ tridivaṃ brahmalokaṃ; nādharmataḥ saṃjaya kāmaye tat
english: Whatever wealth exists in this world, whatever belongs to the thirty gods in the realm beyond — the world of Prajāpati, the triple heaven, the realm of Brahman — none of that do I desire, O Saṃjaya, if it must come through adharma.

sanskrit: dharmeśvaraḥ kuśalo nītimāṃś cāpy; upāsitā brāhmaṇānāṃ manīṣī nānāvidhāṃś caiva mahābalāṃś ca; rājanyabhojān anuśāsti kṛṣṇaḥ
english: Kṛṣṇa is master of dharma, skilled, versed in statecraft, devoted to brāhmaṇas, and wise; he governs kings of many kinds and great might, the Rājanya chiefs who enjoy royal fare.

sanskrit: yadi hy ahaṃ visṛjan syām agarhyo; yudhyamāno yadi jahyāṃ svadharmam mahāyaśāḥ keśavas tad bravītu; vāsudevas tūbhayor arthakāmaḥ
english: If I, by renouncing, would be blameless, or if by fighting I would abandon my own dharma — let the greatly renowned Keśava declare that; Vāsudeva, who desires the welfare of both sides.

sanskrit: śaineyā hi caitrakāś cāndhakāś ca; vārṣṇeyabhojāḥ kaukurāḥ sṛñjayāś ca upāsīnā vāsudevasya buddhiṃ; nigṛhya śatrūn suhṛdo nandayanti
english: The Śaineyas, Caitrakās, Andhakas, Vārṣṇeya-Bhojas, Kaukuras, and Sṛñjayas — abiding by Vāsudeva's counsel, they curb their enemies and delight their friends.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇyandhakā hy ugrasenādayo vai; kṛṣṇapraṇītāḥ sarva evendrakalpāḥ manasvinaḥ satyaparākramāś ca; mahābalā yādavā bhogavantaḥ
english: The Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, Ugrasena and the others, all led by Kṛṣṇa and equal to Indra himself — the Yādavas, high-minded, of true valour, immensely powerful, and wealthy in pleasures.

sanskrit: kāśyo babhruḥ śriyam uttamāṃ gato; labdhvā kṛṣṇaṃ bhrātaram īśitāram yasmai kāmān varṣati vāsudevo; grīṣmātyaye megha iva prajābhyaḥ
english: Babhru of the Kāśī line has attained the highest prosperity, having obtained Kṛṣṇa, the lord, as his brother — Vāsudeva rains down desires upon him, as a cloud at the end of summer rains upon all creatures.

sanskrit: īdṛśo 'yaṃ keśavas tāta bhūyo; vidmo hy enaṃ karmaṇāṃ niścayajñam priyaś ca naḥ sādhutamaś ca kṛṣṇo; nātikrame vacanaṃ keśavasya
english: Such indeed is Keśava, dear one — moreover, we know him as one who discerns with certainty the right course of action; Kṛṣṇa is dear to us and the most righteous of all. I do not transgress the word of Keśava.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca avināśaṃ saṃjaya pāṇḍavānām; icchāmy ahaṃ bhūtim eṣāṃ priyaṃ ca tathā rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya sūta; sadāśaṃse bahuputrasya vṛddhim
english: Vāsudeva said: O Saṃjaya, I desire the imperishable prosperity of the Pāṇḍavas and their welfare; and I always wish for the flourishing of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O sūta, who has many sons.

sanskrit: kāmo hi me saṃjaya nityam eva; nānyad brūyāṃ tān prati śāmyateti rājñaś ca hi priyam etac chṛṇomi; manye caitat pāṇḍavānāṃ samartham
english: My desire, O Saṃjaya, is always just this — I would say nothing other than 'let there be peace' to them; and I hear that this is also dear to the king. I consider this to be equally proper for the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: suduṣkaraś cātra śamo hi nūnaṃ; pradarśitaḥ saṃjaya pāṇḍavena yasmin gṛddho dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputraḥ; kasmād eṣāṃ kalaho nātra mūrcchet
english: But the peace shown here is certainly very hard to achieve, O Saṃjaya — the Pāṇḍava has demonstrated it. Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his sons are greedy for what belongs to them; why then should their quarrel not intensify here?

sanskrit: tattvaṃ dharmaṃ vicaran saṃjayeha; mattaś ca jānāsi yudhiṣṭhirāc ca atho kasmāt saṃjaya pāṇḍavasya; utsāhinaḥ pūrayataḥ svakarma yathākhyātam āvasataḥ kuṭumbaṃ; purākalpāt sādhu vilopam āttha
english: You, O Saṃjaya, roaming here in search of the truth of dharma, know it from me and from Yudhiṣṭhira both. Then why do you speak of the proper disruption, according to an earlier settled principle, of a Pāṇḍava who is energetic, who fulfils his own duty as declared, and who maintains his household?

sanskrit: asmin vidhau vartamāne yathāvad; uccāvacā matayo brāhmaṇānām karmaṇāhuḥ siddhim eke paratra; hitvā karma vidyayā siddhim eke nābhuñjāno bhakṣyabhojyasya tṛpyed; vidvān apīha viditaṃ brāhmaṇānām
english: While this ordinance holds as it should, the opinions of the brāhmaṇas are many and varied: some declare fulfilment in the hereafter through action; some others, abandoning action, declare fulfilment through knowledge. A learned man who does not partake of food and drink cannot be satisfied — that is what is established and known among the brāhmaṇas here.

sanskrit: yā vai vidyāḥ sādhayantīha karma; tāsāṃ phalaṃ vidyate netarāsām tatreha vai dṛṣṭaphalaṃ tu karma; pītvodakaṃ śāmyati tṛṣṇayārtaḥ
english: The branches of learning that accomplish action in this world — their fruit is attainable, not that of the others. In this matter, action has a visible fruit here: just as one afflicted by thirst is appeased after drinking water.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ vidhir vihitaḥ karmaṇaiva; tad vartate saṃjaya tatra karma tatra yo 'nyat karmaṇaḥ sādhu manyen; moghaṃ tasya lapitaṃ durbalasya
english: This ordinance is prescribed through action alone; action abides within it, O Saṃjaya. Whoever in that context deems something other than action to be good — that weak person's chatter is in vain.

sanskrit: karmaṇāmī bhānti devāḥ paratra; karmaṇaiveha plavate mātariśvā ahorātre vidadhat karmaṇaiva; atandrito nityam udeti sūryaḥ
english: It is through action that the gods shine in the world beyond; it is through action alone that the wind blows here below; apportioning night and day through action itself, the sun rises without cease, ever untiring.

sanskrit: māsārdhamāsān atha nakṣatrayogān; atandritaś candramā abhyupaiti atandrito dahate jātavedāḥ; samidhyamānaḥ karma kurvan prajābhyaḥ
english: The moon, untiring, traverses the months, the fortnights, and the conjunctions of the lunar mansions; the fire, untiring and blazing, burns and performs its action for all creatures.

sanskrit: atandritā bhāram imaṃ mahāntaṃ; bibharti devī pṛthivī balena atandritāḥ śīghram apo vahanti; saṃtarpayantyaḥ sarvabhūtāni nadyaḥ
english: Untiring, the goddess Earth bears this great burden by her strength; untiring, the rivers swiftly carry their waters, satisfying all living beings.

sanskrit: atandrito varṣati bhūritejāḥ; saṃnādayann antarikṣaṃ divaṃ ca atandrito brahmacaryaṃ cacāra; śreṣṭhatvam icchan balabhid devatānām
english: Untiring, the one of abundant splendour sends down rain, filling the atmosphere and heaven with its sound; untiring, Indra, the slayer of Bala, practised brahmacharya, desiring pre-eminence among the gods.

sanskrit: hitvā sukhaṃ manasaś ca priyāṇi; tena śakraḥ karmaṇā śraiṣṭhyam āpa satyaṃ dharmaṃ pālayann apramatto; damaṃ titikṣāṃ samatāṃ priyaṃ ca etāni sarvāṇy upasevamāno; devarājyaṃ maghavān prāpa mukhyam
english: Having forsaken ease and the mind's pleasures, Śakra attained supremacy through that action; guarding truth and dharma vigilantly, practising self-restraint, forbearance, equanimity, and affection — cultivating all these, Maghavan won the chief sovereignty of the gods.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir brahmacaryaṃ cacāra; samāhitaḥ saṃśitātmā yathāvat hitvā sukhaṃ pratirudhyendriyāṇi; tena devānām agamad gauravaṃ saḥ
english: Bṛhaspati practised brahmacharya with composure, his mind sharpened, in the proper manner; having forsaken ease and controlled his senses, he thereby attained honour among the gods.

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇi karmaṇāmutra bhānti; rudrādityā vasavo 'thāpi viśve yamo rājā vaiśravaṇaḥ kubero; gandharvayakṣāpsarasaś ca śubhrāḥ brahmacaryaṃ vedavidyāḥ kriyāś ca; niṣevamāṇā munayo 'mutra bhānti
english: The lunar mansions shine in that realm through action; the Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, and the All-gods too; King Yama, Vaiśravaṇa Kubera; the bright Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Apsarases — and sages who practise brahmacharya, the knowledge of the Vedas, and rites shine in that realm as well.

sanskrit: jānann imaṃ sarvalokasya dharmaṃ; brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśāṃ ca sa kasmāt tvaṃ jānatāṃ jñānavān san; vyāyacchase saṃjaya kauravārthe
english: Knowing this dharma of all the worlds — of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas — why is it that you, O Saṃjaya, being knowledgeable among those who know, still exert yourself on behalf of the Kauravas?

sanskrit: āmnāyeṣu nityasaṃyogam asya; tathāśvamedhe rājasūye ca viddhi saṃyujyate dhanuṣā varmaṇā ca; hastatrāṇai rathaśastraiś ca bhūyaḥ
english: Know that he is perpetually joined to the sacred recitations, as also to the Aśvamedha and Rājasūya; he is joined likewise to the bow, to armour, to wrist-guards, and further to the weapons of the chariot.

sanskrit: te ced ime kauravāṇām upāyam; adhigaccheyur avadhenaiva pārthāḥ dharmatrāṇaṃ puṇyam eṣāṃ kṛtaṃ syād; ārye vṛtte bhīmasenaṃ nigṛhya
english: If the Pārthas should find a means of dealing with the Kauravas without slaying them — by restraining Bhīmasena in noble conduct — then a meritorious protection of dharma would be accomplished for them.

sanskrit: te cet pitrye karmaṇi vartamānā; āpadyeran diṣṭavaśena mṛtyum yathāśaktyā pūrayantaḥ svakarma; tad apy eṣāṃ nidhanaṃ syāt praśastam
english: But if, while engaged in their ancestral duty and fulfilling their own task to the best of their ability, they should meet death by the decree of fate — that death too would be praiseworthy for them.

sanskrit: utāho tvaṃ manyase sarvam eva; rājñāṃ yuddhe vartate dharmatantram ayuddhe vā vartate dharmatantraṃ; tathaiva te vācam imāṃ śṛṇomi
english: Or do you think that the entire principle of dharma for kings rests in battle, or alternatively that the principle of dharma rests in non-battle? That is just how I understand this speech of yours.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyasya prathamaṃ vibhāgam; avekṣya tvaṃ saṃjaya svaṃ ca karma niśamyātho pāṇḍavānāṃ svakarma; praśaṃsa vā ninda vā yā matis te
english: Having considered the primary division of the four varṇas, O Saṃjaya, and having heard your own duty, then consider the Pāṇḍavas' own duty — praise it or censure it, as your mind inclines.

sanskrit: adhīyīta brāhmaṇo 'tho yajeta; dadyād iyāt tīrthamukhyāni caiva adhyāpayed yājayec cāpi yājyān; pratigrahān vā viditān pratīcchet
english: A brāhmaṇa should study, then perform sacrifice, give gifts, and go to the foremost of holy tīrthas; he should teach others, officiate at the sacrifices of those fit to sacrifice, or receive lawful gifts.

sanskrit: tathā rājanyo rakṣaṇaṃ vai prajānāṃ; kṛtvā dharmeṇāpramatto 'tha dattvā yajñair iṣṭvā sarvavedān adhītya; dārān kṛtvā puṇyakṛd āvased gṛhān
english: Similarly, a kṣatriya, having protected his subjects with dharma and vigilance, and having given gifts, performed sacrifices, studied all the Vedas, and taken a wife — doing meritorious deeds, he should dwell in his household.

sanskrit: vaiśyo 'dhītya kṛṣigorakṣapaṇyair; vittaṃ cinvan pālayann apramattaḥ priyaṃ kurvan brāhmaṇakṣatriyāṇāṃ; dharmaśīlaḥ puṇyakṛd āvased gṛhān
english: A vaiśya, after studying, should diligently accumulate wealth through agriculture, cattle-herding, and trade, and protect it without negligence; doing what is pleasing to brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas, devoted to dharma, performing meritorious deeds, he should dwell in his household.

sanskrit: paricaryā vandanaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ; nādhīyīta pratiṣiddho 'sya yajñaḥ nityotthito bhūtaye 'tandritaḥ syād; eṣa smṛtaḥ śūdradharmaḥ purāṇaḥ
english: Service and reverence to brāhmaṇas — a śūdra should not study; sacrifice is prohibited for him; he should always rise early for the welfare of others and be untiring — this is remembered as the ancient dharma of the śūdra.

sanskrit: etān rājā pālayann apramatto; niyojayan sarvavarṇān svadharme akāmātmā samavṛttiḥ prajāsu; nādhārmikān anurudhyeta kāmān
english: A king, guarding these carefully and vigilantly, engaging all the varṇas in their own dharmas, free from self-seeking desire, impartial towards his subjects, should not indulge unrighteous desires.

sanskrit: śreyāṃs tasmād yadi vidyeta kaś cid; abhijñātaḥ sarvadharmopapannaḥ sa taṃ duṣṭam anuśiṣyāt prajānan; na ced gṛdhyed iti tasmin na sādhu
english: If one wiser than that, endowed with full knowledge of all dharmas, were to be found, he should discipline the offender, knowing him fully; but if he would not do so out of covetousness — that is not good in such a person.

sanskrit: yadā gṛdhyet parabhūmiṃ nṛśaṃso; vidhiprakopād balam ādadānaḥ tato rājñāṃ bhavitā yuddham etat; tatra jātaṃ varma śastraṃ dhanuś ca indreṇedaṃ dasyuvadhāya karma; utpāditaṃ varma śastraṃ dhanuś ca
english: When a cruel man, defying ordinance and seizing power, covets another's land — from that arises this war among kings. Armour, weapon, and bow were created there for that purpose; this deed was set in motion by Indra for the slaying of brigands — armour, weapon, and bow.

sanskrit: steno hared yatra dhanaṃ hy adṛṣṭaḥ; prasahya vā yatra hareta dṛṣṭaḥ ubhau garhyau bhavataḥ saṃjayaitau; kiṃ vai pṛthak tvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putre yo 'yaṃ lobhān manyate dharmam etaṃ; yam icchate manyuvaśānugāmī
english: Where a thief steals wealth unseen, or where he takes it by force in the open — both of these are blameworthy, O Saṃjaya. What distinction do you make, then, regarding Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son who, driven by greed and following anger's sway, takes this as dharma?

sanskrit: bhāgaḥ punaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ niviṣṭas; taṃ no 'kasmād ādadīran pare vai asmin pade yudhyatāṃ no vadho 'pi; ślāghyaḥ pitryaḥ pararājyād viśiṣṭaḥ etān dharmān kauravāṇāṃ purāṇān; ācakṣīthāḥ saṃjaya rājyamadhye
english: The Pāṇḍavas' portion is established; others have seized it from us without cause. In our situation, even death in battle is praiseworthy — the ancestral domain is superior to another's kingdom. Declare these ancient dharmas of the Kauravas, O Saṃjaya, in the midst of the court.

sanskrit: ye te mandā mṛtyuvaśābhipannāḥ; samānītā dhārtarāṣṭreṇa mūḍhāḥ idaṃ punaḥ karma pāpīya eva; sabhāmadhye paśya vṛttaṃ kurūṇām
english: Those foolish and slow-witted men who have come under the sway of death and have been assembled by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — this deed again is even more sinful. Look at what the Kurus have done in the midst of the assembly.

sanskrit: priyāṃ bhāryāṃ draupadīṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ; yaśasvinīṃ śīlavṛttopapannām yad upekṣanta kuravo bhīṣmamukhyāḥ; kāmānugenoparuddhāṃ rudantīm
english: The beloved wife of the Pāṇḍavas, Draupadī, renowned and endowed with noble character and conduct — the Kauravas, with Bhīṣma at their head, stood by and ignored her when she was being constrained and violated by one driven by lust, weeping.

sanskrit: taṃ cet tadā te sakumāravṛddhā; avārayiṣyan kuravaḥ sametāḥ mama priyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'kariṣyat; putrāṇāṃ ca kṛtam asyābhaviṣyat
english: If the assembled Kauravas, with their young men and elders, had then restrained him, Dhṛtarāṣṭra would have done what is dear to me, and it would have been a deed accomplished for his sons.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaḥ prātilomyān nināya; sabhāmadhye śvaśurāṇāṃ ca kṛṣṇām sā tatra nītā karuṇāny avocan; nānyaṃ kṣattur nātham adṛṣṭa kaṃ cit
english: Duḥśāsana dragged Kṛṣṇā in an outrageous manner into the midst of the assembly, even before her fathers-in-law; brought there, she spoke piteously, seeing no other protector than Vidura.

sanskrit: kārpaṇyād eva sahitās tatra rājño; nāśaknuvan prativaktuṃ sabhāyām ekaḥ kṣattā dharmyam arthaṃ bruvāṇo; dharmaṃ buddhvā pratyuvācālpabuddhim
english: All who were there in that assembly, out of dependence on the king, were unable to speak in reply; only Vidura, speaking the righteous cause and understanding dharma, answered back to the man of little wisdom.

sanskrit: anuktvā tvaṃ dharmam evaṃ sabhāyām; athecchase pāṇḍavasyopadeṣṭum kṛṣṇā tv etat karma cakāra śuddhaṃ; suduṣkaraṃ tad dhi sabhāṃ sametya yena kṛcchrāt pāṇḍavān ujjahāra; tathātmānaṃ naur iva sāgaraughāt
english: Without having spoken thus for dharma in that assembly, you now wish to instruct the Pāṇḍava. But Kṛṣṇā performed this pure and extraordinarily difficult deed — entering that assembly and from that ordeal rescuing the Pāṇḍavas, and herself as well, as a ship rescues from the ocean's flood.

sanskrit: yatrābravīt sūtaputraḥ sabhāyāṃ; kṛṣṇāṃ sthitāṃ śvaśurāṇāṃ samīpe na te gatir vidyate yājñaseni; prapadyedānīṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya veśma parājitās te patayo na santi; patiṃ cānyaṃ bhāmini tvaṃ vṛṇīṣva
english: Where the son of the sūta spoke in the assembly, to Kṛṣṇā standing there near her fathers-in-law: 'O Yājñasenī, you have no refuge; go now to the house of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Your husbands are defeated — they no longer exist as husbands. O beautiful one, choose yourself another husband.'

sanskrit: yo bībhatsor hṛdaye prauḍha āsīd; asthipracchinmarmaghātī sughoraḥ karṇāc charo vāṅmayas tigmatejāḥ; pratiṣṭhito hṛdaye phalgunasya
english: That which was deeply lodged in Bībhatsu's heart — bone-splitting, vital-point-piercing, terrifying — the sharp-flamed arrow of words, shot from Karṇa's mouth, fixed itself in Phalguna's heart.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇājināni paridhit samānān; duḥśāsanaḥ kaṭukāny abhyabhāṣat ete sarve ṣaṇḍhatilā vinaṣṭāḥ; kṣayaṃ gatā narakaṃ dīrghakālam
english: As she stood wearing deer-hide garments, Duḥśāsana spoke harsh words: 'All of these are ruined, seedless like impotent sesame — they have gone to ruin, they will go to hell for a long time.'

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaḥ śakunir nikṛtyā; yad abravīd dyūtakāle sa pārthān parājito nakulaḥ kiṃ tavāsti; kṛṣṇayā tvaṃ dīvya vai yājñasenyā
english: The king of Gāndhāra, Śakuni, by trickery, said this at the time of the dicing to the Pārthas: 'Nakula is defeated — what do you have left? Stake Yājñasenī Kṛṣṇā in the game.'

sanskrit: jānāsi tvaṃ saṃjaya sarvam etad; dyūte 'vācyaṃ vākyam evaṃ yathoktam svayaṃ tv ahaṃ prārthaye tatra gantuṃ; samādhātuṃ kāryam etad vipannam
english: You know all this, O Saṃjaya — this speech that was unspeakable in a game of dice, spoken just so. As for me, I myself intend to go there and to resolve this ruined matter.

sanskrit: ahāpayitvā yadi pāṇḍavārthaṃ; śamaṃ kurūṇām atha cec careyam puṇyaṃ ca me syāc caritaṃ mahodayaṃ; mucyeraṃś ca kuravo mṛtyupāśāt
english: If I can bring about peace for the Kauravas without sacrificing the Pāṇḍavas' cause, then my conduct would be meritorious and of great benefit, and the Kauravas would be freed from the noose of death.

sanskrit: api vācaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya kāvyāṃ; dharmārāmām arthavatīm ahiṃsrām avekṣeran dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ samakṣaṃ; māṃ ca prāptaṃ kuravaḥ pūjayeyuḥ
english: Would the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra attend to the eloquent speech I would speak — delighting in dharma, purposeful, and non-violent — and would the Kauravas honour me when I arrived in their presence?

sanskrit: ato 'nyathā rathinā phalgunena; bhīmena caivāhavadaṃśitena parāsiktān dhārtarāṣṭrāṃs tu viddhi; pradahyamānān karmaṇā svena mandān
english: Otherwise, know that the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — sprinkled with arrows by the chariot-warrior Phalguna and by Bhīma, armoured for battle — are fools being consumed by their own deed.

sanskrit: parājitān pāṇḍaveyāṃs tu vāco; raudrarūpā bhāṣate dhārtarāṣṭraḥ gadāhasto bhīmaseno 'pramatto; duryodhanaṃ smārayitvā hi kāle
english: The son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra speaks fierce words to the Pāṇḍavas who were defeated; but Bhīmasena, mace in hand, vigilant, will in due time remind Duryodhana of those words.

sanskrit: suyodhano manyumayo mahādrumaḥ; skandhaḥ karṇaḥ śakunis tasya śākhāḥ duḥśāsanaḥ puṣpaphale samṛddhe; mūlaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'manīṣī
english: Suyodhana is a great tree made of wrath; its trunk is Karṇa, Śakuni its branches; Duḥśāsana is the flower and fruit in full abundance; the root is King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that man of no wisdom.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro dharmamayo mahādrumaḥ; skandho 'rjuno bhīmaseno 'sya śākhāḥ mādrīputrau puṣpaphale samṛddhe; mūlaṃ tv ahaṃ brahma ca brāhmaṇāś ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira is a great tree made of dharma; its trunk is Arjuna, Bhīmasena its branches; the two sons of Mādrī are the flower and fruit in full abundance; but the root is I, and brahman, and the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: vanaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputro; vyāghrā vane saṃjaya pāṇḍaveyāḥ mā vanaṃ chindhi savyāghraṃ mā vyāghrān nīnaśo vanāt
english: King Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his sons is the forest; the Pāṇḍavas, O Saṃjaya, are the tigers in that forest. Do not cut down the forest that contains its tigers; do not destroy the tigers away from the forest.

sanskrit: nirvano vadhyate vyāghro nirvyāghraṃ chidyate vanam tasmād vyāghro vanaṃ rakṣed vanaṃ vyāghraṃ ca pālayet
english: Without a forest, the tiger is slain; without tigers, the forest is cut down. Therefore the tiger should protect the forest, and the forest should shelter the tiger.

sanskrit: latādharmā dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ śālāḥ saṃjaya pāṇḍavāḥ na latā vardhate jātu anāśritya mahādrumam
english: The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are of the nature of creepers; the Pāṇḍavas, O Saṃjaya, are the great Śāla trees. A creeper does not grow without clinging to a great tree.

sanskrit: sthitāḥ śuśrūṣituṃ pārthāḥ sthitā yoddhum ariṃdamāḥ yatkṛtyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya tat karotu narādhipaḥ
english: The Pārthas are prepared to serve; those tamers of enemies are also prepared to fight. Whatever Dhṛtarāṣṭra should do — let that lord of men do it.

sanskrit: sthitāḥ śame mahātmānaḥ pāṇḍavā dharmacāriṇaḥ yodhāḥ samṛddhās tad vidvan nācakṣīthā yathātatham
english: The great-souled Pāṇḍavas, who walk in dharma, stand committed to peace; they are warriors in full strength — knowing this, O wise one, do not report it other than as it truly is.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca āmantraye tvā naradevadeva; gacchāmy ahaṃ pāṇḍava svasti te 'stu kaccin na vācā vṛjinaṃ hi kiṃ cid; uccāritaṃ me manaso 'bhiṣaṅgāt
english: Saṃjaya said: I take my leave of you, O god among men, O Pāṇḍava; I am going — may all be well with you. I hope I have not spoken any harsh or injurious word through my tongue's attachment to my mind.

sanskrit: janārdanaṃ bhīmasenārjunau ca; mādrīsutau sātyakiṃ cekitānam āmantrya gacchāmi śivaṃ sukhaṃ vaḥ; saumyena māṃ paśyata cakṣuṣā nṛpāḥ
english: Having taken leave of Janārdana, Bhīmasena, Arjuna, the two sons of Mādrī, Sātyaki, and Cekitāna — I depart. May all be auspicious and pleasant for you. Look upon me with a gentle eye, O kings.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anujñātaḥ saṃjaya svasti gaccha; na no 'kārṣīr apriyaṃ jātu kiṃ cit vidmaś ca tvā te ca vayaṃ ca sarve; śuddhātmānaṃ madhyagataṃ sabhāstham
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Go with our leave, Saṃjaya — go in well-being. You have never done anything displeasing to us. We know you, as you know us, and we all know you — pure in soul, standing in the middle, established in the assembly.

sanskrit: āpto dūtaḥ saṃjaya supriyo 'si; kalyāṇavāk śīlavān dṛṣṭimāṃś ca na muhyes tvaṃ saṃjaya jātu matyā; na ca krudhyer ucyamāno 'pi tathyam
english: You are a trusted envoy, O Saṃjaya, and very dear to us; you speak auspiciously, are virtuous, and endowed with insight. You, O Saṃjaya, are never confused in your understanding, and you do not grow angry even when truth is spoken to you.

sanskrit: na marmagāṃ jātu vaktāsi rūkṣāṃ; nopastutiṃ kaṭukāṃ nota śuktām dharmārāmām arthavatīm ahiṃsrām; etāṃ vācaṃ tava jānāmi sūta
english: You never speak words that pierce to the vital point and are harsh; nor hollow flattery, nor bitter reproach. I know your speech, O sūta, to be this: delighting in dharma, purposeful, and non-violent.

sanskrit: tvam eva naḥ priyatamo 'si dūta; ihāgacched viduro vā dvitīyaḥ abhīkṣṇadṛṣṭo 'si purā hi nas tvaṃ; dhanaṃjayasyātmasamaḥ sakhāsi
english: You are the one most dear to us as envoy; Vidura would be the second who might come here. For you were seen often among us in former times; you are a friend equal to Dhanañjaya's own self.

sanskrit: ito gatvā saṃjaya kṣipram eva; upātiṣṭhethā brāhmaṇān ye tadarhāḥ viśuddhavīryāṃś caraṇopapannān; kule jātān sarvadharmopapannān
english: On your way from here, O Saṃjaya, go quickly and attend upon those brāhmaṇas who are worthy of it — those of pure vigour, endowed with right conduct, born in noble families, and possessed of all dharmas.

sanskrit: svādhyāyino brāhmaṇā bhikṣavaś ca; tapasvino ye ca nityā vaneṣu abhivādyā vai madvacanena vṛddhās; tathetareṣāṃ kuśalaṃ vadethāḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas devoted to Vedic recitation, those who live by alms, and the ascetics who dwell permanently in the forests — the elders among these should be saluted with my words; and to the rest enquire about their welfare.

sanskrit: purohitaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rājña; ācāryāś ca ṛtvijo ye ca tasya taiś ca tvaṃ tāta sahitair yathārhaṃ; saṃgacchethāḥ kuśalenaiva sūta
english: The purohita of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the ācāryas, and the officiating priests who serve him — together with them, dear one, meet as is fitting and with all due propriety, O sūta.

sanskrit: ācārya iṣṭo 'napago vidheyo; vedān īpsan brahmacaryaṃ cacāra yo 'straṃ catuṣpāt punar eva cakre; droṇaḥ prasanno 'bhivādyo yathārham
english: The beloved teacher who did not abandon, who was obedient — desiring the Vedas, he practised brahmacharya; he who restored the science of weapons in its fourfold completeness — may Droṇa, when he is pleased, be saluted as is proper.

sanskrit: adhītavidyaś caraṇopapanno; yo 'straṃ catuṣpāt punar eva cakre gandharvaputrapratimaṃ tarasvinaṃ; tam aśvatthāmānaṃ kuśalaṃ sma pṛccheḥ
english: He who has mastered learning, is endowed with right conduct, who has restored the science of weapons in its fourfold completeness — the swift one who is like the son of a Gandharva: do enquire after Aśvatthāman's welfare.

sanskrit: śāradvatasyāvasathaṃ sma gatvā; mahārathasyāstravidāṃ varasya tvaṃ mām abhīkṣṇaṃ parikīrtayan vai; kṛpasya pādau saṃjaya pāṇinā spṛśeḥ
english: Going to the dwelling of Śāradvatī's son, the great chariot-warrior, foremost among those who know the science of weapons — repeatedly proclaiming my name, O Saṃjaya, touch with your hand the feet of Kṛpa.

sanskrit: yasmiñ śauryam ānṛśaṃsyaṃ tapaś ca; prajñā śīlaṃ śrutisattve dhṛtiś ca pādau gṛhītvā kurusattamasya; bhīṣmasya māṃ tatra nivedayethāḥ
english: In whom reside valour, compassion, ascetic power, wisdom, noble character, truth in learning and being, and steadfastness — clasping the feet of Bhīṣma, the best of the Kurus, announce me to him there.

sanskrit: prajñācakṣur yaḥ praṇetā kurūṇāṃ; bahuśruto vṛddhasevī manīṣī tasmai rājñe sthavirāyābhivādya; ācakṣīthāḥ saṃjaya mām arogam
english: He whose eye is wisdom, the guide of the Kurus, widely learned, devoted to the service of elders, and sagacious — having paid your respects to that venerable king, tell him, O Saṃjaya, that I am in good health.
